question: If Y + 1over{}z = 1 and X + 1over{}y = 1, then what is the value of XYZ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

From **X + 1/Y = 1**, we get **X = (Y − 1)/Y**.

From **Y + 1/Z = 1**, we get **1/Z = 1 − Y**, which means **Z = 1/(1 − Y)**.

Multiply **X**, **Y**, and **Z**: **XYZ = [(Y − 1)/Y] × Y × [1/(1 − Y)]**.

**XYZ = (Y − 1) / (1 − Y) = −1**.

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **Y + 1/Z = 1** and **X + 1/Y = 1**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3788191c14909e6f498d6f819c495b8ac58b27b71e3517987125c4792f01cae.png] 

⇒ From the first equation: **X + 1/Y = 1**

⇒ **X = 1 − 1/Y**

⇒ **X = (Y − 1) / Y**

⇒ From the second equation: **Y + 1/Z = 1**

⇒ **1/Z = 1 − Y**

⇒ **Z = 1 / (1 − Y)**

⇒ Now calculate **XYZ**: **XYZ = [(Y − 1) / Y] × Y × [1 / (1 − Y)]**

⇒ **XYZ = (Y − 1) / (1 − Y)**

⇒ **XYZ = −(1 − Y) / (1 − Y) = −1**

**∴ The correct answer is −1.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cyclic Algebraic Expressions

In a set of **cyclic equations** like **a + 1/b = 1** and **b + 1/c = 1**, the third relation is typically **c + 1/a = 1** and the product **abc = −1**.

Variable Substitution

When solving **multi-variable equations**, expressing all terms in respect to a **single common variable** (like Y in this case) is the most efficient method to find products or sums.

Negative Unity Property

Note that **(a − b) / (b − a) = −1**. This identity is frequently used to simplify fractions in **algebraic simplification** questions.</p
